Self-improving products is a meta idea every company should be implementing.  

Some of the core pieces you will need:

1/ a crisp definition of the various metrics you care about : primary, secondary, guardrail

2/ an articulation of your strategy, roadmap and metrics you care about moving the most

3/ knowledge base of past product decisions and principles so the agent knows how decisions get made 

4/ connections to your to your internal product systems: dashboards, APIs, MCPs, and tools your agent  needs to observe and act on your product. 

5/ a harness built with knowledge of  your end to end product development flow. 

Depending on the complexity of your product, you might be able to prototype with fairly simple versions of each of the above and reuse existing swe agents.

One non-model thing I'm very excited we announced today with Fable 5.1 is Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS).

Even if you're not a CEO/CISO, this blog post is a look into how big companies are thinking about AI adoption which is important to understand if you're interested in how AI might diffuse across industry.

tweets.text:
Sometimes people don’t have an intuitive sense of what Jevons paradox looks like for token consumption. Those of us working with enterprises get to see this first hand every day.

Basically enterprises have an unending stream of tasks that they’d love to be able to bring automation to. But for each individual task, it’s either ROI positive or not based on the cost of bringing automation to it (including the setup time, change management, and so on).

As tokens get cheaper (at a certain capability threshold), enterprises can afford bringing them to more of the work that they do. This could be processing every contract, reading every log, watching new streams of data for insights, having background agents execute workflows, and so on. 

Any time we can lower the cost of tokens, we will see a disproportionate increase in consumption. Even a 50% drop in token prices could result in a 5X increase in tokens for these kinds of workloads.

This is why it’s critical to keep bringing down the cost of AI, and why that’s good for all market participants.
tweets.summary_zh:
有些人不太理解“杰文斯悖论”（指的是资源变便宜时，使用量反而会急剧增加）在企业使用机器人处理工作的时候的表现。企业们总是希望能自动化更多的任务，但每个任务是否划算，主要取决于自动化的费用。

随着机器人处理成本的降低，企业能用它们来处理更多的工作，比如分析合同、查看日志、监测数据等。每当降低这些成本，就会看到使用量大幅增加，甚至价格下降50%可能导致任务使用量增加五倍。

因此，持续降低AI的成本，对所有参与者都是有益的。

AI product building has a ~3-month playbook half-life. Here’s how to adapt.

Most trad product teams are built to discover a playbook and then milk it for the next 5 years.

However in the AI labs, we consciously throw away playbooks every few months cos we start seeing diminishing returns.

Here’s what you can do as an AI builder:

Focus on defining a set of meta-principles for 
1/ how you continuously learn what the market wants today and what it might want in 3 months
2/ how you execute with extreme urgency

The specifics of 1 and 2 will vary based on your domain and product type.
Build a team that learns and adapts at that pace. 

Legacy teams are optimized for playbook milking.

AI teams need to be optimized for inventing.

This week’s tech earnings calls were a critical reminder of how valuable the relationship is between software and AI.

Software provides the guardrails for how data is managed, how business logic in workflows are maintained, how you manage and govern access to information, how you protect data, and more. You want these systems to work the same way every time, without fail. 

Agents, on the other hand, work inside these systems and with this data to execute on tasks just like people would have. But at a scale far greater than people ever did, which is especially why the deterministic controls matter more than ever.  

And in fact many of the best ways to deploy agents will be directly within the software systems themselves, like from Salesforce, Box, Harvey, ServiceNow, and so on. These platforms can optimize agents for their workflows and domains, with evals and context that are unique to their vertical, as well as connect to other 
 agents headlessly. 

The net result is both software and AI adoption go up, hand in hand. Software and Agents are going to work together, and ultimately grow the size of the IT TAM dramatically as a result over time.

tweets.text:
Yesterday, at Box we reported our Q2 results with revenue of $321.1 million for the quarter, up 9%, or 11% in constant currency (our highest constant-currency growth rate in 14 quarters), and we raised our full-year revenue target to $1.290 billion. Overall, this growth is being driven by the demand we're seeing from enterprises aiming to get the most out of their enterprise content and transform in the era of AI.

As I shared on our earnings call, during the quarter I spoke with many enterprise technology leaders who highlighted their primary goals and challenges in implementing AI. One of the most common topics is how enterprises can get the right context to AI agents, as well as tap into the full value of their unstructured data, in a secure and governed way.

The world’s most advanced superintelligence is only as useful as the underlying enterprise knowledge it has access to. Agents need access to the critical information that makes up the bulk of corporate knowledge --like contracts, research materials, financial documents, marketing assets, product roadmap information, and so on-- most of which lives within an enterprise’s unstructured data.

We've long been able to query, calculate, and automate work that deals with structured data; but the vast majority of data in an enterprise is unstructured, often in the form of our enterprise content. Instead of sitting on millions or hundreds of millions of files they know very little about, companies can now use AI agents to ask questions about this data, mine it all for intelligence, and automate nearly any workflow that involves this enterprise content.

The technology leaders I'm talking to are also recognizing that as AI model capabilities advance across AI labs --like OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceXAI, Meta, Google, NVIDIA, and a variety of open-weight providers-- they will need applied AI platforms that can bring the full power of these models to their processes. And with AI token usage continuing to grow exponentially, the ability to draw the right cost-performance mix becomes essential. Rather than migrating data and workflows into separate systems to unlock AI's benefits, enterprises need the ability to swap models or agents on their workflows and information at any time.

Finally, as we saw with the recent OpenAI Hugging Face incident, enterprises will increasingly need platforms that can securely protect their corporate data and ensure that neither humans nor agents can get access to information they shouldn’t have access to. As external AI agents interact with enterprise data, enterprises will need platforms that offer robust guardrails, comprehensive audit logs, and real-time security alerts to ensure content remains protected and governed at all times.

Given all of these dynamics, there's going to be a tremendous amount of opportunity for various plays to bring intelligence to the critical workflows inside of enterprises at the applied AI layer. At Box. we're focused on building the leading intelligent content management platform to empower enterprises to transform how they work with their unstructured data at scale. And we're looking forward to partnering with all of the other companies bringing intelligence into organizations as well.

Today, I’m open-sourcing /fuck-cancer, an AI skill that helps patients and caregivers navigate cancer diagnosis and treatment and advocate for themselves and their loved ones.

Here’s what patients and caregivers have told me since I shared my mom’s story:

“You have to be a huge patient advocate. Ask questions and push for answers, biopsies, and proper testing.”

“I need help navigating difficult conversations and advocating for myself.”

“The volume of doctors, documents, and insurance paperwork can quickly become overwhelming.”

I built the skill to help with these problems. It creates and updates a practical brief with five sections:

1. Patient and care-team information for easy reference during calls

2. What to do next, limited to three specific actions

3. What we know, separating confirmed facts from what remains unclear

tweets.text:
How to build great evals — Part 9

The Eval Roadmap Problem 

Most evals fail because teams treat them as static artifacts while their users  expectations and behaviors have evolved.
 
Your evals need a roadmap that evolves with your product and actual usage patterns.

Take a financial research agent. Here is how use cases will evolve over time.

Early user: Summarize this 5-page earnings report.

3 weeks later: review the last 5 earnings reports and explain their growth story.

2 months later: Here are 15 filings, earnings transcripts and research reports. Build an investment thesis.

Eventually: Monitor my stock portfolio and tell send me alerts when something materially changes my thesis.

Each stage requires different capabilities and hence different evals.

Your evals should change with usage patterns:

short-context -> long-context
single-turn QA -> multi-turn
passage citations -> doc and line citations 
Simple QA -> complex synthesis
reactive chat -> proactive agent

If your evals are stuck in week 1 while users are in week 3, it will show in your product and churn metrics.

Here’s a practical way to build the roadmap:
1/ Map the dimensions along which usage will evolve (eg # turns, document size, tool use, autonomy, journey coverage).
2/ Prioritize the use cases and dimensions that matter most for your product.
3/ Talk to your users, mine production traces to look for shifts.
4/ Build P0 evals for the next stage of usage.
5/ Run the evals, find failure modes (remember the taxonomy from Part 3), and hill-climb (from part 6).

The goal is to stay ahead of usage patterns. PM 101.

Drop your questions and I will address in future posts.

Share this with your teammates who think your evals are perfect.

builders.bio: Claude is an AI assistant built by @anthropicai to be safe, accurate, and secure. Talk to Claude on https://t.co/ZhTwG8d1e5 or download the app.

tweets.text:
Topics some consider sensitive, like health or religious beliefs, stay out of memory unless you turn them on in Settings.

Memory is on by default on Free, Pro, and Max plans. Review yours anytime in Settings > Memory.

Read more: https://t.co/2y4B3am1RX
tweets.summary_zh: 一些人觉得敏感的话题，比如健康或宗教信仰，不会被记住，除非你在设置中开启这个功能。免费、专业和高级套餐默认开启记忆功能，你随时可以在设置里查看。

tweets.text:
Everything Claude remembers is saved as a list of topics in Settings, where you can read, edit, or delete each one.

Memory also updates on its own as you chat, saving new details as they come up. You can also say "remember this" to save something specific. https://t.co/ExpQAHkyhu
tweets.summary_zh: Claude 现在能够记住你聊过的内容，这些记忆会自动更新，你可以在设置里查看、编辑或删除。你也可以告诉它“记住这个”，来特别保存一些信息。

tweets.text:
Claude now has one memory across chat and Claude Cowork, and you decide what's in it.

Hand Cowork a task and it starts from what Claude already knows from your chats: the project you talked through, your manager's preferences, or the client from last quarter. https://t.co/ViKapsT8K6
tweets.summary_zh: Claude 现在可以记住你在聊天和 Claude Cowork 上的内容，而且你可以决定保存哪些信息。给 Claude Cowork 交代任务时，它会参考你以前聊天中提到的内容，比如你讨论过的项目、老板的偏好或上个季度的客户。

github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个现代化的格式化库，主要用于简化和优化文本的输出和显示，比如格式化字符串。对Yves的TexTale电商业务特别有帮助，因为在电商平台上，良好的文本格式可以提升产品展示的专业性和吸引力，同时作为创意设计从业者，他也可以利用这个工具来创建更个性化和吸引人的品牌内容。

github_trending.description: TimesFM (Time Series Foundation Model) is a pretrained time-series foundation model developed by Google Research for time-series forecasting.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个由谷歌研究团队开发的预训练时间序列模型，主要用于预测未来的时间序列数据，比如销售趋势或市场波动。对Yves来说，这个项目可以为TexTale提供数据驱动的销售预测帮助，从而优化电商运营策略，同时作为创意设计从业者，也可以利用这个模型分析趋势数据，提升设计灵感和决策效果。

github_trending.description: Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
github_trending.summary_zh:
这个项目名为 ponytail，旨在让你的 AI 助手以一种懒散的高级开发者的方式思考，强调“最好的代码就是你从未编写的代码”，也就是尽量减少人工编写的代码量。 

对 Yves 来说，这个项目可能会对 Logic Labs（AI 公司）产生帮助，因为它可以优化 AI 助手的效率，提升工作流程，使创意设计过程更加流畅高效。

github_trending.description: VoiceStudio is the open-source, fully-local ElevenLabs alternative — voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription & audiobook creation in 646 languages.
github_trending.summary_zh: VoiceStudio 是一个开源工具，允许用户在本地进行语音克隆、语音设计、视频配音、听写、转录和有声书创作，支持多达 646 种语言。这个项目可以帮助 Yves 的 Logic Labs（AI 公司）提升人工智能语音技术的应用，尤其在创意设计和内容创作方面，同时也可以为 TexTale（科技服装电商）提供个性化的语音营销和客户互动体验。作为创意设计从业者，Yves 可以利用 VoiceStudio 实现更加生动和吸引人的创意内容，提升品牌影响力。

github_trending.description: A股自动选股系统 — 多种技术形态自动扫描，收盘后自动运行并推送飞书
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个自动化的股票选股工具，可以通过不同的技术指标来扫描股票市场，并在每天市场收盘后自动运行，通知用户。对于Yves来说，这个项目可能对Logic Labs（AI公司）更有帮助，因为它展示了如何利用AI技术进行高效的数据分析，帮助他在AI行业趋势和应用上获得灵感。同时，这种自动化思路也可启发他在创意设计和电商运营中寻找更智能化的解决方案。
这个项目是为开发者提供的一个工具，可以帮助他们创建和调试代码，尤其是涉及到机器学习和人工智能的应用。对Yves来说，Logic Labs（AI公司）可以直接受益，因为这个工具能提高团队在开发AI相关项目时的效率和创意实现。此外，作为创意设计从业者，Yves也能利用这个工具更好地理解和运用AI技术，推动设计创新。

github_trending.description: The agent that grows with you
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个智能代理，能够根据用户的需求和习惯进行不断学习和适应，从而提供个性化的服务和支持。对于Yves来说，这个项目可以在Logic Labs（AI公司）中帮助提升AI模型的智能化和用户体验，也能为TexTale（科技服装电商）提供更好的客户洞察和个性化营销策略，增强品牌竞争力。作为创意设计从业者，这个工具还可以激发新的创意灵感，提升设计效率。

github_trending.description: Open-source inference server and production cluster for all the models your agent needs.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个开源的平台，帮助用户运行各种 AI 模型，以便为智能代理提供支持和推理能力。对于Yves来说，这个项目特别对Logic Labs有帮助，可以增强其AI产品的性能和效率，同时也能为TexTale提供更加智能的电商解决方案，如个性化推荐与用户体验优化。作为创意设计从业者，Yves可以利用这个平台加速创意过程，开发更加智能化的设计工具。

github_trending.description: Source control for agents. Use multiple coding agents, track their changes and query them in one place
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个源代码管理工具，专门用于管理和跟踪多个编码智能体的变化，让用户可以在一个地方查询和协作。对Yves来说，这个项目可以帮助Logic Labs（AI公司）更有效地组织和协作开发与AI相关的项目，提高创新效率，同时也能够为TexTale在电商平台上整合AI工具提供技术支持，优化用户体验。作为创意设计从业者，Yves可以利用这个工具更好地管理和追踪创意实现过程中的灵感和版本变化。

github_trending.description: Practice English, one strike, one step forward; 练习英语，一次敲击，一点进步；
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个基于 Vue 的英语练习工具，用户可以通过简单的敲击键盘来逐步提高自己的英语水平。对于Yves来说，TypeWords可以帮助他在Logic Labs中探索如何利用 AI 技术提升教育产品的用户体验，同时也能为TexTale提供创意灵感，拓展科技与教育相结合的电商营销策略。
